log: RETIRING A FOLLOW-UP I PROPOSED -- can saturating kinetics rescue the dose-response?
loop 5 failed V3 and I wrote a specific follow-up into it. A named follow-up that never gets
tested is an excuse with a citation, so this tests it -- and the argument comes first.
THE ARGUMENT.  With one K shared by all enzymes, capacity(f) = E*f/(f+K) evaluates every
gene's curve at f' = f/(f+K) -- the SAME constant for every gene. The family of curves is
unchanged; only the point on the dose axis moves. AUC is rank-based, so the ranking cannot
change. If that is right, the AUC at 50%, 25% and 10% must be nearly identical.
dose point                AUC
50% capacity           0.5087
25% capacity           0.5075
10% capacity           0.5053
0% (knockout)          0.5529
Q1 THE INVARIANCE HOLDS -- spread across the three dose points 0.0033  (gate <= 0.02)   Q1 PASS
Moving along the dose axis changes the ranking by less than the gate. A uniform
saturating kinetic does exactly that and nothing else, so it CANNOT rescue V3.
The follow-up is retired on principle, not on appetite.
Q2 WHAT WOULD BE NEEDED -- gene-specific saturation, i.e. a different K per enzyme.
cell_complete blocks carrying kinetics : NONE of the 42
per-gene fields carrying kinetics      : NONE of the 27
genes with a usable per-enzyme constant : 0   (gate >= 200)   Q2 FAIL
There are modules here ABOUT kcat -- biochem_limit tries to predict it, apply_kcat_fixes
corrects flagged values -- but no per-gene constant reaches cell_complete, and none of
the 42 blocks or the gene fields carries one. The only version of this idea that could
change the answer needs a different K for every enzyme, and that quantity is not in
this container.
Q1 the invariance holds                 PASS
Q2 gene-specific kinetics available     FAIL
THE FOLLOW-UP IS RETIRED, WITH A REASON.  A uniform saturating kinetic provably cannot
change loop 5's answer -- it only slides the dose axis, and the three dose points show
that sliding it changes nothing. The one version that COULD work needs a per-enzyme
saturation constant, which does not exist here. loop_variant's proposed follow-up should
not be attempted again on this data, and that is worth more than leaving it open.
